item.title: Coldcard hardware wallet flaw let attacker drain 594 BTC (~$38M) from about 500 wallets in under 30 minutes on July 31.
Crypto exploits have totaled roughly $972M so far in 2026, per year-to-date industry tracking data.
Bitcoin and Ethereum-linked protocols lost $35M across multiple attacks occurring within hours on July 23.
Arbitrum-based AFX Trade lost $24M in USDC after attackers used compromised hot-validator signatures to approve a withdrawal.
DeFi protocol Ostium lost $18M in USDC after an oracle attack manipulated price-feed timestamps to trigger fraudulent payouts.
U.S. federal agencies missed the July 18 GENIUS Act deadline to finalize stablecoin rules, with no binding regulations issued.
SEC plans to propose three crypto rules in July covering token offerings, broker-dealer custody, and digital-asset trading venues.
The Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act faces a Senate make-or-break vote before August; failure likely kills the bill for this year.
MiCA's transitional period ended July 1, forcing EU crypto-asset service providers without full licenses to halt operations.
Tether's USDT has a two-year countdown to gain GENIUS Act compliance before U.S. platforms must remove non-compliant stablecoins.
BNY Mellon's European unit joined the EU's MiCA licensed CASP register in the third post-deadline update, expanding licensed coverage.
The EU is rewriting core parts of MiCA one year after its July 1 full-compliance deadline as the framework undergoes review.
Morgan Stanley received preliminary OCC approval in June to establish a national trust bank for digital-asset custody and staking.
JPMorgan began accepting Bitcoin ETF shares, including BlackRock's IBIT, as collateral for loans following GENIUS Act enactment.
High MiCA compliance costs are expected to drive M&A consolidation in the European crypto sector, benefiting licensed banks.
